items.title: Kane the hero on historic night as England book Nations League QF spot
items.excerpt: Record-breaker Harry Kane scored from the spot to seal England's place in the Nations League quarter-finals with a 2-1 victory over Croatia, capping a memorable Wembley night as the captain became his country's most-capped player.
body: Record-breaker Harry Kane scored from the spot to seal England's place in the Nations League quarter-finals with a 2-1 victory over Croatia, capping a memorable Wembley night as the captain became his country's most-capped player.

There was an inevitability about Kane hitting the net on his 126th appearance. There had been pre-match tributes and accolades as the Ballon d'Or holder passed the mark of legendary goalkeeper Peter Shilton and once again Kane was England's match winner with his second-half spot-kick. That's 92 goals now in England colours for the record scorer. As it happened | Match stats | England fixtures Nations League scores & news | Tables | Sky Bet

The win means England will now have the chance to win Nations League Group A3 and be seeded for the quarter-finals - but they will have to be far better than this if they are to beat table-toppers and world champions Spain in Madrid on Sunday.

England thumped Croatia 7-0 last month but this was a performance far shy of that previous display, lacking intensity and final-third spark for long periods, and littered with jittery moments at the back.

Neville believes United have handled the situation poorly, with Carrick taking training in Manchester while club executives met in Monaco on Wednesday and pursued Pochettino as his replacement .

items.title: 'Overwhelming' - Record-breaker Kane celebrates 'amazing' Wembley night
items.excerpt: Harry Kane says the reaction to his Ballon d'Or win and record appearance for England has been "overwhelming".
body: Harry Kane says the reaction to his Ballon d'Or win and record appearance for England has been "overwhelming".

The Three Lions captain walked out at Wembley on Thursday to a huge tifo celebrating his 126th international appearance and received awards from former record holder Peter Shilton, Prince William and Croatia captain Luka Modric, as well as presenting his Ballon d'Or trophy to the crowd.

Kane then went on to strike the winning penalty for England in a 2-1 Nations League triumph which sealed their place in the quarter-finals of the competition. They can top the group and be seeded for the last-eight draw if they beat Spain in Madrid on Sunday.

"It was incredible. Everything was amazing," said Kane in a post-match press conference. "Thank you to everyone who organised [the tributes], with the tifo and presentations. items.title: Kane makes history with record 126th England cap
items.excerpt: Harry Kane has broken the record for the most senior England caps by a single player in history.
body: Harry Kane has broken the record for the most senior England caps by a single player in history.

The Three Lions captain led the line for Thursday's Nations League game against Croatia, making his 126th appearance for his country in the process and scoring his 92nd goal to win the game at Wembley .
He bypassed the record previously held by goalkeeper Peter Shilton, who earned 125 caps between 1970 and 1990.
Shilton paid tribute to Kane on the pitch ahead of kick-off, with Prince William and visiting captain Luka Modric also honouring the England skipper before the game.

items.title: Iraola: We must sacrifice control for creativity to fix scoring woes
items.excerpt: Liverpool must sacrifice control in games in order to fix their creativity problems, Andoni Iraola has demanded ahead of their weekend trip to Crystal Palace, live on Sky Sports .
body: Liverpool must sacrifice control in games in order to fix their creativity problems, Andoni Iraola has demanded ahead of their weekend trip to Crystal Palace, live on Sky Sports .
The Reds have created the second-fewest big chances in the Premier League this season and scored only four goals in five home games, their joint-fewest at this stage of a season in their history.

They set an unwanted record against Arsenal last weekend , failing to register a shot on target in a home Premier League game for the first time in more than 440 games since Opta records began in 2003.

Iraola arrived at Anfield last summer with a reputation for front-foot, direct football but has had difficulties imposing his philosophy on his new players in the first three months of the season, and now wants them to take more risks to turn their domination into clear-cut opportunities.
